concepts.title: Rotation of the Earth
concepts.definition: The spinning movement of the Earth around its own imaginary axis, which takes approximately 24 hours to complete.
concepts.key_idea: Rotation causes the daily cycle of day and night.

concepts.title: Revolution and Leap Year
concepts.definition: The Earth's orbital movement around the Sun, taking 365.25 days, where the extra quarter-days accumulate to form a leap year every four years.
concepts.key_idea: Revolution causes seasonal changes and the leap year cycle.

solution_steps.explain: Standard year is 365 days, plus 0.25 days per year.

concepts.title: Solstice and Equinox
concepts.definition: Solstices are points in the orbit where one hemisphere receives maximum sunlight, while equinoxes are points where the Sun shines directly on the equator.
concepts.key_idea: Tilt of the Earth's axis relative to the orbital plane determines seasonal intensity.

solution_steps.explain: Solstice involves maximum tilt towards/away from the Sun; Equinox involves zero tilt relative to the Sun's rays at the equator.
